title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is section 1.3 of a dictionary of 'equivalent data'. The previous page (§1.7) treats the non-split, Borel-type case; this page treats the split, torus-type case. Together they set up the language for connections on P^1-bundles with a section, that is, projective structures and uniformisations, as needed for Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs (§1.8 and the next page).

Over a base X the following data are claimed equivalent:

(1) A P^1-bundle P → X with two disjoint sections σ, σ'.

(2) An invertible sheaf Ω. Then P = P(Ω ⊕ O_X) is the projective closure of the line bundle W(Ω) = V(Ω), with σ the section at infinity and σ' the zero section. Ω is recovered as the normal bundle of one of the sections, up to the sign/dual convention.

(3) [Probably] the algebra M of rank-4 'operators' (End L, with L = Ω ⊕ O split), now given together with a splitting into two invertible pieces or idempotents.

(4) A Lie algebra g of type A1, a twisted form of pgl2, graded as g ≃ Ω ⊕ Ω^0 ⊕ Ω^{-1} with Ω^0 = O_X. Write λ for sections of O, ω_1 for Ω and ω_{-1} for Ω^{-1}. The brackets are
  [λ, ω_1] = λω_1,
  [λ, ω_{-1}] = −λω_{-1},
  [ω_1, ω_{-1}] = 2 ω_1ω_{-1} ∈ O.
Equivalently, g comes with a Cartan subalgebra t together with a choice of one of the two Borel subalgebras containing t. That choice fixes the isomorphism t ≃ O_X ≃ Hom(Ω, Ω).

(4') For the other integral form g' (Lie SL2-type), the brackets must be rescaled to −2λω_1, 2λω_{-1}, ω_1ω_{-1}. This is the standard h/2 versus h normalisation, which distinguishes Lie(PGL2) from Lie(SL2) over Z and matters in characteristic 2 (the margin note asks about characteristic ≠ 2).

(5) A group G (PGL2-form), and likewise G' (SL2-form), each with a 'couple de Killing' (B, T): a Borel subgroup together with a maximal torus.

The next page uses such a splitting g ≃ Ω ⊕ O ⊕ Ω^{-1} to write a trivial connection and then a general connection plus a 1-form ϖ = ϖ_2 ⊕ ϖ_1 ⊕ ϖ_0. In modern terms this is a local coordinate description of PGL2-bundles with Borel reduction and connection, i.e. projective connections / sl2-opers.
errors: The bracket conventions are self-consistent: with t = h/2 one gets [t,e]=e, [t,f]=−f, [e,f]=2t. Written as [ω_1,λ] = −λω_1 etc., the sign conventions are correct.

The equivalence (3) with an algebra 'somme directe de deux faisceaux inversibles' is too sketchy or illegible to check. As stated it is imprecise: End(Ω ⊕ O) is rank 4, and the splitting corresponds to two complementary idempotents or two rank-2 ideal-like pieces, not just two invertible summands.

ideas.what: P^1-bundle with two disjoint sections ↔ line bundle Ω via P(Ω ⊕ O) = projective closure of V(Ω)
ideas.modern_name: split P^1-bundles / reduction of the PGL2-torsor to the torus G_m
ideas.where_published: EGA II §8 (projective cones / closures of vector bundles)

ideas.modern_name: split reductive group schemes of rank 1 / pinnings-twisted forms; Killing couple (B,T)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3, Exp. XX and XXII ('couple de Killing')

ideas.what: Distinction between the Lie(PGL2) and Lie(SL2) integral forms (factor 2 in brackets), relevant in characteristic 2
ideas.modern_name: non-isomorphic Z-forms of sl2 / adjoint vs simply connected Lie algebras

ideas.what: Using these dictionaries to describe connections on (P, σ) as connections on g with Borel reduction (projective structures for Picard–Fuchs uniformisation)

missed.claim: The surrounding dossier (§1.7–1.8 and the next page) formulates projective connections / uniformisation data as PGL2- and SL2-bundles with Borel reduction and a connection, in a dictionary covering P-bundles, extensions, Lie algebras with Borel and groups with Killing couples, and keeps track of characteristic 2. This is in the spirit of opers, roughly two decades before Beilinson–Drinfeld. This page itself only gives the split (torus) case and is routine.
missed.quote: G avec couple de Killing / G' avec couple de Killing
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possible historical precursor to the oper formalism, including integral and characteristic-2 care (g vs g'). This is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine dictionary of the split case (a line bundle giving a split pgl2 with explicit brackets and a Killing couple), all standard in SGA 3. It is mildly interesting only as part of an oper-like programme for Picard–Fuchs equations.
transcription_corrections: 'fibrés projectifs [?] sur X' is likely 'fibrés projectifs [en droites] sur X avec deux sections disjointes σ, σ''.
Under P = P(Ω+O_X) ≃ closure of W(Ω), the next lines likely read roughly 'clôture projective de W(Ω), avec section à l'infini σ, σ' = section nulle'.
'G avec couple de Killing' and 'G' avec couple de Killing' are the last two lines; 'couple de Killing' is the SGA 3 term.
'le choix d'une des deux sous-algèbres [de Borel] contenant t' is probably the intended reading of the Cartan/Borel line.
The margin probably concerns g' versus g and characteristic ≠ 2.
